questions.q: What is the central argument of the passage?
options: Getting wealthy depends mainly on frugality, while staying wealthy needs bold concentrated bets
Most investors stay wealthy by copying the strategies of legendary traders like Jesse Livermore
Staying wealthy takes survival traits like frugality and paranoia, unlike getting wealthy
Long-term compounding makes picking stocks irrelevant, so luck decides who stays wealthy
questions.explain: The author says there's only one way to stay wealthy: frugality and paranoia, and survival matters most.

questions.q: How did Jesse Livermore profit in the 1929 crash?
options: He sold his real estate
He bought gold
He held only cash
He was short the market
questions.explain: He had bet stocks would decline and made over $3 billion equivalent in one day.

questions.q: Why did Rick Guerin drop out of Buffett and Munger's group?
options: He was levered with margin loans and was forced to sell Berkshire stock in 1973-74
He bet heavily on tech start-ups and was forced to sell his Berkshire stock in 1987
He overpaid for an insurance acquisition and had to sell his Berkshire shares in 1969
He fell out with Munger over a partnership and cashed out his Berkshire stake in 1980
questions.explain: Margin calls in the downturn forced him to sell his Berkshire stock to Warren at under $40.

questions.q: What did Michael Moritz say about why Sequoia has lasted four decades?
options: They've always trusted a handful of star partners to pick winners
They've always been afraid of going out of business
They've never taken on risk outside of proven software markets
They've always avoided companies not already near profitability
questions.explain: He said 'we've always been afraid of going out of business.'

questions.q: According to the author, what is margin of safety?
options: Raising returns at a given level of risk by concentrating in the best ideas
Reducing the odds of failure by diversifying across as many assets as possible
Increasing leverage at a given level of risk to speed up compounding of wealth
Raising the odds of success at a given level of risk by improving the chance of survival
questions.explain: It is distinct from being conservative; it increases survival odds at a given level of risk.
